suggestions: For an injection A/B test, most expectations (E1, E5, E6 especially) quote text that lives verbatim in the injected visual-check SKILL.md / rubric. A PASS therefore mostly proves the injected context was present and recalled, not that the model gained repo understanding. Add at least one expectation targeting a fact NOT in the injected material (e.g., that the config loader stops at the .git boundary, or that measurements.json flags overflow only) so the A vs B contrast is discriminating.

E1 does not pin the path root. `screenshots/<target>/ai-notes.json` is relative to the demo-app cwd; the transcript prefixes `demo-app/`. The expectation should state which root is authoritative so a bare `screenshots/...` answer and a `demo-app/screenshots/...` answer are graded consistently.

The questions.txt instructs the executor to flag uncertainty ('모름/추측'). No expectation rewards calibration/honesty. Consider an expectation that penalizes confidently-stated wrong or unverifiable claims, since that behavior is exactly what the injection is meant to reduce.
eval_feedback.overall: The six expectations are precise, atomic, and each maps to a checkable repo fact; grading was unambiguous and all six passed against ground truth with no imprecision. The main weakness is not the answers but the eval design: it does not isolate 'injected recall' from 'genuine knowledge', which is the whole point of an injected-vs-baseline comparison.
